analysis.title: Early Thoughts On Blue Wave Implications On DC & Power Funding
key_insights: Democrats won both chambers of Congress and governor races in key data center states (Texas, Georgia, New Mexico, Nevada) in the Nov 3 midterms. JPM says this has profound implications for the Data Center and Power sectors.

42 of 45 local ballot measures to restrict data centers have passed or are leaning toward passing. North Dakota (Harwood) is the only one that failed, and two had not posted results. Ohio has the most restrictions (20), followed by Illinois and Maine.

JPM expects more local ballot measures to restrict data centers in 2028. It argues governors-elect are likely to follow through on their platforms, and that a pivot away from them would not be instantaneous.

Governor-elect platforms: Texas (Hinojosa) called for an immediate moratorium. Georgia (Bottoms) called for a statewide pause of one to six months or longer. New Mexico (Haaland) called for a pause on new large projects until guardrails exist. Nevada (Ford) proposed pausing data center tax breaks. Ohio (Acton) proposed a conditional moratorium.

JPM expects weakness across most independent power producers (IPPs), especially those with exposure in Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Georgia (CEG, NRG, TLN, VST and others). New projects face higher approval hurdles, which favors projects already approved.

Behind-the-meter (BTM) and bridge power providers (SEI, VOLTAG) are expected to see the largest near-term negative impact. Longer data center construction timelines could soften demand for bridge power before new grid supply arrives in 2029, particularly in Texas and PJM.

JPM sees a pullback in data center development as relatively benign for regulated utility credit. Data centers have been a 'nice to have' for credit, and a pullback in related capex could ease balance sheet pressure. Capital investment is still expected to grow through at least 2030.

About 27% of the MW of data center capacity funded in the HY project finance market is being built in Texas. About 78% of the tracked pipeline for public HY data center builders is in Texas, mainly Cipher and Galaxy. Risk is concentrated in 2028/29 energizations, which could face delays or terminations.

Neoclouds such as CRWV are exposed to data center build delays, which could delay capacity coming online and affect contract timing. CRWV rents or plans to rent data centers in ND, IL, GA, TX, NC, OK, VA and NY, and owns data centers in PA and NJ.

JPM says built or fully permitted data centers and power assets are worth more than before the election, while new permitting in Texas, Georgia, New Mexico and Nevada will likely be slower and costlier. It does not expect moratoriums to become permanent bans.

JPM expects developers to focus more on receptive states (Louisiana, North Dakota) and on international sites. It does not expect material changes to 2027 capital plans, but expects some impact in 2028 and beyond.

Most 2027 projects are already funded, so the open question is when 2028+ projects get funded. JPM expects bond supply to slow near term, with first new deals focused on 'safe' jurisdictions. The slowdown should relieve some technical pressure on the sector, and a shallower growth curve could keep compute in short supply longer.

market_movers.rationale: JPM calls VST relatively well insulated from a pending moratorium because its 2.6GW Meta project involving nuclear plants in OH and PA is already underway. It still lists VST among IPPs expected to weaken.
JPM expects weakness in IPPs with exposure in Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Georgia. CEG could see higher contracted revenue as existing PPAs come online.
JPM expects IPP weakness after the Democratic wins. NRG has exposure in Texas, though it also has balanced exposure elsewhere, including PJM.
JPM expects IPP weakness after the Democratic wins. TLN could see increased contracted revenue as existing PPAs come online.
Neocloud exposed to data center build delays, which could delay capacity and affect contract timing. It leases sites in several states, including TX and GA.
Much of Cipher's HY data center pipeline is in Texas, which is where JPM sees the most regulatory risk. JPM flags 2028/29 energizations as the most exposed.
JPM says AEP Texas could see tailwinds after it recently doubled its approved data center development in Texas to 1.6GW.
Applied Digital's HY data center projects are mostly in North Dakota, which JPM calls a receptive state. Its Texas pipeline is small (Dorothy 3, 50 MW).

sector_views.rationale: JPM expects weakness after the Democratic wins, especially for IPPs exposed to TX, OH, PA and GA. Contracted PPAs coming online could cushion balance sheets over time.
Largest near-term negative impact expected. Longer construction timelines could cut demand for bridge power before new grid supply arrives in 2029.
Growth expectations may reset, but a pullback in data center capex is relatively benign for credit and could ease balance sheet pressure.
Texas concentration and an uncertain unfunded pipeline raise delay risk. Assets already built or permitted gain value.

crypto_views: Bitcoin-miner-turned-HPC builders (Cipher, TeraWulf, Core Scientific, Galaxy, CleanSpark, Applied Digital) are in JPM's HY data center project finance universe. Cipher and Galaxy account for most of the Texas pipeline exposure.
risk_factors: Texas moratorium or tighter regulation could delay or terminate 2028/29 data center energizations. Termination rights in Figure 3 offset some of this.
Unfunded HY data center pipelines look more uncertain and harder to finance.
Neocloud contract timing could slip if data center builds are delayed.
Local ballot measures could multiply in 2028.
New power generation is not expected until about 2029, so BTM and bridge providers face a gap in demand.
Moratoriums could harden into longer-lasting restrictions, though JPM does not expect permanent bans.
vol_and_positioning: JPM expects bond supply from data center and GPU builders to slow near term, which should ease technical pressure on the sector.
geopolitical: Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, plus governor races in Texas, Georgia, New Mexico and Nevada, in the Nov 3 midterms.
Local ballot measures to restrict data centers passed or are leaning toward passing in 42 of 45 cases, concentrated in the Midwest.
Georgia Senator Jon Ossoff has called for a complete moratorium and an investigation into data center development in Georgia.

tension_points.bull_case: Built and fully permitted assets gain value. A slower buildout keeps compute scarce longer, gives monetization time to catch up with spending, and eases bond supply pressure. Receptive states like Louisiana and North Dakota and international sites may gain developer focus.
tension_points.bear_case: Democratic governors-elect in TX, GA, NM, NV and OH campaigned on pauses or moratoriums, and 42 of 45 local ballot measures are passing. IPPs, bridge power providers and Texas-heavy HY builders such as Cipher and Galaxy face delays, terminations and a harder funding path for 2028+ projects.
tension_points.what_invalidates: JPM does not expect moratoriums to become permanent bans. It says a governor reversing course on a platform would not be instantaneous.
